long_biography.plain_text:
Farkhad Akhmedov first built his commercial footing in London, trading Russian sable on the commodity exchange. He then founded Tansley Trading to supply equipment to Russian gas producers. A minority investment in Nortgas became the decisive shift: after acquiring another shareholder's stake, he took the chairmanship and developed an operating position in Siberian natural gas.

The sale of his remaining Nortgas interest turned an industrial fortune into investment capital. Away from energy, Akhmedov assembled a collection spanning twentieth-century Azerbaijani painting and opened Nar Gallery in Baku to public visitors. Its permanent display has included works by nonconformist artist Ashraf Murad, linking private collecting with the preservation and presentation of an under-recognised national school.
